notes.title: Casebook 1899 is out! Watch me play!
notes.notes: [p]🕵️‍♂️ [b]Casebook 1899 – The Leipzig Murders is Available Now on Steam![/b] 🕰️[/p][p]I'm thrilled to announce that [b]Casebook 1899 – The Leipzig Murders[/b] is officially released and available for purchase on Steam![/p][p]Step into the shoes of [b]Detective Joseph Kreiser[/b] and delve into the heart of a beautifully crafted, historically inspired mystery. Set in [b]Leipzig, Germany at the turn of the 20th century[/b], this richly atmospheric [b]point-and-click detective adventure[/b] invites you to uncover the truth behind a string of murders in a city on the brink of modernity.[/p][p]Explore [b]hand-pixellated environments[/b], painstakingly designed with attention to historical detail, and immerse yourself in a narrative-driven experience where [b]every clue, conversation, and choice matters[/b].[/p][p]In its first week you can get the game at an [b]10 % discount[/b]![/p][hr][/hr][p]🕯️ [b]What Awaits You in Casebook 1899:[/b][/p][p]🔎 [b]Investigate Four Gripping CriminalCases[/b] Navigate crime scenes, examine evidence, and interrogate witnesses as you piece together each case across four standalone investigations—each with multiple possible outcomes depending on your deductions.[/p][p]📖 [b]Your Notebook is Your Greatest Tool[/b] Track your findings, analyze witness statements, and link clues together on your [b]deduction board[/b] to reveal hidden connections and uncover the true culprit.[/p][p]🎙️ [b]Authentic Voice Acting[/b] Fully voiced in [b]German[/b] for authenticity, with subtitles available in [b]English, German, and Italian[/b].[/p][p]🧠 [b]Your Choices Shape the Story[/b] Choose your suspects carefully—there are [b]no game overs[/b], just the consequences of your reasoning. Each decision can change the outcome, and only the most observant detectives will reveal the full truth.[/p][p]🎮 [b]Classic Point-and-Click Gameplay[/b] Perfect for fans of story-driven mystery games, historical adventures, and anyone who loves a good puzzle with a strong narrative backbone.[/p][hr][/hr][p]Casebook 1899 is more than just a mystery—it's a journey into a rarely explored chapter of European history, wrapped in a compelling detective narrative and brought to life with stunning pixel art and atmospheric sound design.[/p][p][/p]

notes.title: Solve mysterious murders in Casebook 1899 - The Leipzig Murders with a launch set for September
notes.notes:
Casebook 1899 - The Leipzig Murders is a richly atmospheric, retro-inspired point-and-click adventure set in Leipzig, Germany at the dawn of the 20th century.

Read the full article here: https://www.gamingonlinux.com/2025/08/solve-mysterious-murders-in-casebook-1899-the-leipzig-murders-with-a-launch-set-for-september/

notes.title: Casebook 1899 is coming September 4
notes.notes: [p]I'm very excited to reveal that [i]Casebook 1899 - The Leipzig Murders [/i]launches on PC, Mac and Linux on [b]September 4[/b].[/p][p][/p][p]Step into the role of Detective Joseph Kreiser in four weeks as you explore the fog-shrouded streets of Leipzig and unravel four gripping murder cases.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]Watch the new trailer[/b][/h3][p][/p][previewyoutube="appNvUWjeg8;full"][/previewyoutube][p][/p][p]Explore hand-pixellated scenes inspired by meticulous historical research. Examine clues, interrogate witnesses, and solve environmental puzzles as you navigate a city gripped by change and shadowed by crime. Your notebook and deduction board are essential tools—combine evidence, draw your own conclusions, and unmask the true culprit across four gripping murder cases.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]German Voice Acting, English and Italian texts[/b][/h3][p]All dialogues in the game are fully voiced in German. Text is available in English and Italian, with more languages to follow after release.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]Uncover vital evidence[/b][/h3][p]Scour beautifully hand-pixellated environments for hidden clues, brought to life with detailed, handcrafted animations. Each scene captures the atmosphere of a bustling 19th-century Leipzig, Germany.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]Interrogate suspects and witnesses[/b][/h3][p]Cross paths with witnesses and suspects alike—but it's up to you to tell them apart. Gain their trust, ask the right questions, and uncover what they’d rather keep hidden.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]Use your notebook[/b][/h3][p]Keep track of every observation and witness statement in your notebook, where each scene has its own dedicated page for easy reference when you need it most.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]Draw your own conclusions[/b][/h3][p]Combine clues in your notebook to unlock new conclusions on your deduction board. Piece together the facts and identify the true culprit from a list of suspects.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]Your choices will matter[/b][/h3][p]Your choice of culprit in each of the four cases determines the outcome, making this a true test of your deductive skills. A sharp eye and keen mind are your greatest weapons in the fight against crime.[/p]

notes.title: Updated Demo released for a limited time only!
notes.notes:
I have just released an updated demo that better represents the game in its current state.
It has quality of life improvements like the interfaces (inventory, main menu, notebook) being controllable with mouse alone, keyboard alone (no mouse-wheel necessary) or a mix of the two. This includes a button for opening the main menu on the top-right corner.
Speaking of the main menu - that has also been completely redesigned to better fir the theme and interfaces of the game.
There are a lot of improvements to the games graphics as well. The only thing that separates it from the finished game is the voice acting. Some of the roles will be re-recorded by professional voice actors as promised in the Kickstarter.
Oh, and this demo includes the complete first case of the game. But this will change the closer we will get to the release date. So better be quick if you want to see if you can correctly solve the first case.

notes.title: AdventureX Developer Stream
notes.notes:
Are you craving for adventure game news? Do you want to see some of the most beautiful pixels ever put on a computer screen? Can't you ever get enough of snappy dialogue options?
If you answered any or all of these questions with "YES" then AdventureX in London is just the place to be. I know it's the place where I will be this weekend. But if you can't make it to London then this stream might be for you:
I will show you a very spoilery playthrough of the third case of Casebook 1899 - The Leipzig Murders. I will explain why it really the second case of the game and what went into the design of some of the puzzles. As a bonus I will show you the one puzzle where I am unsure if I got the best solution to it.
But I will repeat this: this stream will have SO MANY SPOILERS! So if you don't want any spoilers better make sure the game is on your wishlist and sit this one out!

Also, if you want to save tons on great adventure games or discover new ones, have a look at the #AdvX23 event page!

[url=https://store.steampowered.com/sale/AdventureX2023][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41657396/8d47e43ec1cb62cac50379f4ff820ef48a1fd25a.png[/img][/url]

The stream will be repeated several times over the weekend.

notes.title: LAST CHANCE: Steam Mystery Fest Developer Stream
notes.notes:
Steam Mystery Fest has started so it is high time for a new developer stream.
This time I will not be playing much of the game but instead I will give update to the status of the game.
I will also get into details and show some early scenes from case 2 and 3. If you don't want any spoilers, it might be best to skip this stream!
We will talk about Visionaire Studio and some of the challenges of development that I have overcome in the last few weeks. We will also update the schedule for the development and you will learn where you will be able to play an exclusive demo of the second case next.

notes.title: Livestream: Casebook 1899 @ AdventureX 2022
notes.notes:
Some while ago Casebook 1899 has been picked to be one of the games to be exhibited at AdventureX in London. This is of course an incredible honour as I will be able to show the game next to the absolutely best upcoming adventure games.

[b]Exclusive demo![/b]
In order to stand out I am not only bringing some cool swag to the show floor but I have worked very hard for the last few weeks to bring a NEW and EXCLUSIVE demo with me. So if you want to be one of the few people who wants to play a short excerpt from the SECOND case of Casebook 1899, you better pack for the big city!

[b]Leipzig in Greenwich![/b]
If you are able to come to the event be sure to stop by the Casebook 1899 stand and say hello! You can find me both days at the Stockwell Street Building at the University of Greenwich.

[b]New insights in exclusive stream![/b]
If you're not able to come down to London, you should make sure to tune in to the developer streams. You will also be able to see some new content!

notes.title: Casebook 1899 - The Leipzig Murders: Demo out now! Crowdfunding live!
notes.notes:
[h3]Play the first case NOW[/h3]
To celebrate the start of the crowdfunding campaign for Casebook 1899 - The Leipzig Murders you can now play the [b]complete first case for free[/b]!
Head on over to the demo and dive into a German boomtown at the end of the 19th century.

[h3]Leipzig at the end of the 19th century[/h3]
Like every day, Detective Inspector Joseph Kreiser tells his landlady Hannah Faber about the day's experiences. And this time he has an incredible tale to tell: When he is called to a traffic accident in the industrial quarter of the city, he meets an old friend, the public prosecutor Gustav Möbius. Investigating the case, it quickly becomes clear that this is no normal traffic accident. Is there even a murder charge at the end of the case?
That's up to you to find out in [b]Joseph Kreiser's first case: Madcap Motorist[/b]!

[h3]Crowdfunding[/h3]
You can support the production of the full game with three more cases here:
[url=bit.ly/3rWd2T5]Casebook 1899 on Kickstarter[/url]

[h3]Features[/h3]
[list]
[*]Classic point-and-click adventure
[*]Inventory and environment puzzle
[*]Witness interrogations and dialogue trees
[*]Combine clues in your notebook and draw conclusions
[*]No game-overs
[*]5 different endings - success depends on your talent as a detective
[*]Complete German voice-over
[*]Subtitles in English and German
[*]Find clues and interrogate suspects in accurately researched historical locations
[*]Focus on dialogue and interaction
[*]50 minutes of gameplay
[/list]

notes.title: Casebook 1899 loves the Tux and Demo-Release-Date
notes.notes:
Good news, Linux-Lovers! 
[h3][b]Casebook 1899 - The Leipzig Murders[/b] will be coming to [b]Linux[/b] as well. [/h3]
And the best news is that it won't be tied to any stretch goals of the upcoming crowdfunding, it will happen just like that!
Of course the free demo will also come to Linux.

Speaking of... The date for the release of the demo is set as well!
[h3][b]You will be able to play the complete first case from May 31![/b][/h3]

To celebrate the start of the crowdfunding I will release the first case FOR FREE.

The demo will:
[list]
[*]be available for PC, Mac and Linux
[*]offer around 50 minutes of gameplay
[*]let you explore a German boomtown at the end of the 19th century
[*]be fully voiced in German
[*]offer subtitles in German and English
[*]get your "little grey cells" [b]really[/b] working
[/list]
Hope you will download the demo and be convinced to get involved in the crowdfunding that starts the same day!
